The Engineering Lead, David Taylor, suggested improvements to the Technical Specifications Document for CollaborateForce, including enhancing AI capabilities to provide more advanced insights, expanding integration options to include a wider range of tools, and strengthening marketing efforts to increase adoption and user engagement. These recommendations aim to position the product as a leader in collaborative data-driven discussions.

The QA Specialist suggested adding specific accuracy benchmarks for AI insights in the Functional Requirements section, including achieving at least 95% accuracy in data trend predictions and 90% accuracy in anomaly detection. They recommended including performance metrics such as response times under 2 seconds for data queries and under 1 second for user interface interactions in the Non-Functional Requirements section. For Integration Requirements, they suggested detailing specific integration scenarios or use cases, such as automatically generating and sharing AI-driven insights in Slack channels and initiating Zoom meetings directly from data dashboards. In the Security and Compliance section, they advised mentioning ISO 27001 certification. Lastly, they recommended listing potential new tools or platforms for future integration, such as Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, and Asana, in the Recommendations section.

The NLP engine enhancement in FeedbackForce includes upgrading to the latest version of TensorFlow, integrating BERT for enhanced language understanding, retraining models with BERT, implementing model quantization for size reduction, and optimizing the inference pipeline for speed. These improvements were implemented through several PRs, including 'Upgrade TensorFlow to Latest Version', 'Integrate BERT for Enhanced Language Understanding', 'Retrain Models with BERT', 'Implement Model Quantization for Size Reduction', and 'Optimize Inference Pipeline for Speed'. However, the optimization for speed was later reverted due to security vulnerabilities. The feature was discussed and implemented in multiple product-planning meetings.

The new features added to FeedbackForce for integration with enterprise systems include support for JSON and XML formats, a middleware layer for format conversion, and specific implementations such as JSON to XML conversion middleware and XML to JSON conversion middleware. These features ensure consistency with existing middleware and introduce robust error handling and logging mechanisms. Additionally, the integration includes efforts to optimize the middleware for high-volume data processing and to integrate the middleware with enterprise system interfaces, although the latter is still pending merge.

The new features added to FeedbackForce for compliance with GDPR and CCPA include the implementation of role-based access controls (RBAC) to manage permissions for accessing sensitive information, as well as the establishment of a framework for conducting regular security audits. These features were implemented through the PRs 'Establish Access Controls for Sensitive Information' (PR:https://github.com/salesforce/backAIX/pull/12) and 'Conduct Regular Security Audits' (PR:https://github.com/salesforce/backAIX/pull/19). Additionally, there was a discussion and implementation effort for AES-256 encryption for data in transit, though this PR remains open and unmerged.

The features that could not be added to FeedbackForce due to security risks include implementing AES-256 encryption for data in transit, as the PRs for this feature (PR:https://github.com/salesforce/backAIX/pull/6 and PR:https://github.com/salesforce/backAIX/pull/9) were not merged and remain open with pending action. Additionally, the feature 'compliance with GDPR and CCPA' was marked as implemented but reverted, indicating that some security-related implementations were rolled back due to unresolved risks.
